chunks: The Shaykh Abū ʿAbd Allāh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Bābawayh, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb and al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb together, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq, from Hārūn ibn Ḥamzah al-Ghanawī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a mouse, a scorpion, and the like falling into water and then coming out alive: may that water be drunk from and wudu (ablution) performed from it? He said: It should be poured out three times, and its small amount and large amount are of one rank; then one may drink from it and perform wudu (ablution) from it, except for the gecko, for no benefit is taken from what it falls into. And we have already spoken about this report previously.

key_terms.الْعَقْرَبِ: a scorpion mentioned in the ruling alongside similar creatures
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse mentioned as one of the creatures falling into the water
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: the water being discussed for drinking and wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْوَزَغِ: the gecko, excluded from the permissibility mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.يُسْكَبُ: it is poured out, here specified as three times

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on water if a mouse or scorpion falls into it and comes out alive?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding water into which a mouse, scorpion, or similar creature falls and emerges alive. It states that the water may be used for drinking and wudu (ablution) after pouring it out three times, with an exception made for the gecko, whose contact renders what it falls into unusable.
